basics.name: Vasco Kaufmann Figueiredo
basics.label: Co-Founder & CTO @UpSpeech
basics.summary:
Co-founder and CTO of UpSpeech, based in Lisbon. I've spent six years shipping Rails and React products at agencies, at a health-tech startup and on my own. Away from the keyboard I play and watch basketball.

I build with AI agents every day. Claude Code writes most of my code while I own the architecture, the reviews and the tests, and I've built my own skills and hooks around how I work. I also put LLMs into products people use. Therapy Resources draws illustrations in each therapist's own style, and Cadence Studio runs a team of agents that draft in the writer's voice and wait for approval before anything goes out.

projects.description: A content studio for one person. A small team of agents writes posts in your voice on a schedule you set, and nothing publishes until you approve it. Every draft gets checked against 16 rules and a 27-word watchlist of AI tells before it reaches the review queue. It switches between Claude, Gemini and OpenAI models through the Vercel AI SDK and makes images with fal.ai. Built with React, TypeScript and Convex, and in private beta.

Therapists pick an illustration style once, then generate cards, board games and worksheets in it. Gemini draws the illustrations to match the style, a Konva canvas editor handles layout, and the app exports print-ready PDFs. 162 therapists have signed up and made 470 resources, in English and Portuguese. Built with Next.js, TypeScript and Convex.

Basketball stats for leagues and teams, with live scoring, shot charts and heatmaps, player comparisons and automatic standings. It has 697 accounts, 307 of them active in the last 30 days, and 750 downloads across the iOS and Android apps. One Turborepo holds the React web app and the React Native app, both on a Convex backend that updates in real time.

A free, open-source desktop app for basketball coaches that I built and maintain. Coaches cut game film into tagged clips, sort them into categories and export them for the team. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux and has about 1,000 installer downloads. Built with Electron, React, TypeScript and FFmpeg.

work.name: UpSpeech
work.summary: Co-founded a speech therapy platform for clinics that treat stuttering. I built the Rails API, the React web app and the React Native app, including multi-tenant accounts, session management, patient progress tracking and deployment. Working with Claude Code, I've merged over 2,700 pull requests across them since September 2025. As CTO I own the architecture and product direction, and I work with our AI lead on the transcription and report-writing service.

work.name: Pixelmatters
work.summary: Placed with UJET.cx, a cloud contact center platform, building features in Ruby on Rails and Angular. I got the end-to-end tests running in local development, so the team could catch integration bugs before CI, and helped new engineers get their setup working. I led the backend of the Deflection Audio project and mentored a teammate through their first feature. I also brought AI tooling to the team, first Augment Code and then my own Claude Code skills for shipping and code review, which colleagues started using. Promoted to senior (L3) in May 2026.

work.name: Medihive
work.summary: Worked mostly in Ruby on Rails on a cross-functional team. I built internal tools, including the admin and doctor panels, and features on the client-facing site in ERB and some React. Over time I took on whole features from start to production, and the company promoted me to senior developer.

work.name: BitZesty
work.summary: Worked fully remote in Ruby on Rails on a cross-functional team. Each client ran a different Ruby and Rails version, and the job was finding the fix that fit their budget. I upgraded several apps from Rails 5 to Rails 6.

work.name: Landing.jobs
work.summary: My first developer job. I went from junior to mid-level in a year, working in Ruby on Rails, React, TypeScript and GraphQL, and won the company's Revelation of the Year award for 2020.

work.name: Accenture Portugal
work.summary: VBA tools and a Customer Care & Billing system in Java.

work.name: WeDo Technologies
work.summary: Logic-based development in RAID, the company's in-house tool. WeDo is now Mobileum.
